objects.name: Chipkin Example B-LD
objects.note: the device itself; the instance is configurable with --deviceID. The stack rows are device-wide facts only the stack knows - the protocol version and revision it implements, the services and object types it was configured with, the live object list and address-binding table. The accepted rows are the stack's configured defaults for APDU limits, segmentation, system status and database revision; an application that answered them from its own constants could contradict the stack, so this example does not. Local_Date and Local_Time (optional Device properties) have GetPropertyDate/GetPropertyTime callbacks in main.cpp, but nothing calls SetPropertyEnabled for either - so they are never in the object's enabled-property list and the stack answers unknown-property before either callback is reached. See TUTORIAL.md for the details

objects.name: Jade
objects.note: REAL 0-100%; commandable via a 16-slot Priority_Array (WriteProperty/DS-WP-B) AND via the typed Lighting_Command SEQUENCE (DS-LO-B). This is B-LD's canonical F-LIGHT object. The app's lighting engine (main.cpp section 1b) runs every Table 12-67 operation over time: Present_Value is the target, Tracking_Value the level being driven, In_Progress fadeActive/rampActive while it moves, Egress_Active TRUE during a warn's egress time. Reliability (optional, enabled) reports lampFailure from the lamp Simulation and is writable only while Out_Of_Service is TRUE (cl. 12.54.12); the dimming defaults and Egress_Time are writable, range-checked. Last_On_Value and Default_On_Value (required in 135-2024, cl. 12.54.44/45) are served by the app but not rows here because the stack's property-profile reference at this pin does not list them; Current_Command_Priority and Property_List are served by the stack

objects.name: Vermilion
objects.note: BACnet/IP; Network_Type and Protocol_Level are set from BACnetStack_AddNetworkPortObject()'s arguments (IPv4, BACnet Application) at start-up, not a GetProperty callback like the object's other app-served rows; Changes_Pending is likewise computed and answered natively by the stack's Network Port object. Reliability has no fault condition this example detects, so it is accepted at the generic default (normal)
